root_motivation: Every local cargo build recompiles the same heavyweight crates (serde, tokio, clap) from scratch across 190+ repos because sccache is absent; wiring a size-capped sccache with zero shared-lock contention eliminates that waste without the parallel-build serialisation problem that a single CARGO_TARGET_DIR imposes.
user_persona: Joe Yen, developer on an Arch Linux laptop running up to 30 parallel /build ticks; each tick compiles independent Rust crates and re-encounters the same slow dependency compilation. Needs a persistent, size-capped compilation cache that is safe under parallel cargo invocations.

acceptance_criteria.description: `wire` merges `RUSTC_WRAPPER = "sccache"` under `[build]` in the fleet `config.toml` without removing a pre-existing `target-dir` key (verify both keys present after).
`wire` is idempotent: a second run leaves `config.toml` byte-identical.
`wire --max-size 20G` records a 20G cap in the sccache config that `status` reads back as `max_size`.
`unwire` removes only `RUSTC_WRAPPER` (other `[build]` keys preserved), is idempotent, and does not delete the cache directory.
`stats` parses a fixture `sccache --show-stats` output (no live sccache required) into JSON with `cache_hits`, `cache_misses`, and a computed `hit_rate` in `[0,1]`.
`status` reports `installed`, `wired`, `cache_bytes`, `max_bytes` and exits 0 whether or not sccache is actually installed (degrades, does not panic).
`install` with `--local-build` flag available; without cloud/network reachable it fails with a clear actionable message and non-zero exit, never leaves a half-wired config.

scope: CLI binary `hold-sccache` with subcommands: install, wire, unwire, stats, status
Parse/merge TOML config at ~/wintermute/.cargo/config.toml using toml_edit (preserving all existing keys)
Parse `sccache --show-stats` text output into structured JSON
Report installation and wiring status without requiring a live sccache daemon
non_goals: Does not install sccache from source or compile it locally by default
Does not manage the sccache daemon lifecycle (start/stop/restart)
Does not implement the sccache distributed protocol or sccache-dist
Does not modify any per-repo Cargo.toml or per-repo .cargo/config.toml
Does not delete or purge the sccache cache contents (only manages configuration)

five_whys_trace.q: Why does every cargo build recompile serde/tokio/clap from scratch?
five_whys_trace.a: There is no sccache installed (`which sccache` → not found), so cargo has no compilation cache beyond its own per-target incremental artifacts.

five_whys_trace.q: Why not just use a single shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR (like hold-anchor)?
five_whys_trace.a: A single target dir serializes parallel builds via cargo's exclusive lock on it; the user runs up to 30 parallel /build ticks, so this creates a convoy effect.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is sccache the right tool over, say, cargo's built-in caching?
five_whys_trace.a: sccache is a content-addressed compilation cache keyed on compiler inputs (flags + source hash), not the target path; multiple parallel builds with different target/ dirs all share the same cached object files without locking each other.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does this need a CLI wrapper rather than a simple setup script?
five_whys_trace.a: The TOML merge must be idempotent and must not clobber hold-anchor's target-dir key; stats parsing needs structured JSON output; status must degrade gracefully on a machine where sccache is absent — these are ongoing operational concerns, not a one-shot setup.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Which cargo config.toml path? ~/wintermute/.cargo/config.toml or ~/.cargo/config.toml?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: The PRD says ~/wintermute/.cargo/config.toml (fleet config for the wintermute ecosystem), consistent with hold-anchor's target-dir key.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Where does the sccache size cap live?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: In ~/.config/sccache/config as a TOML file with [cache.disk] max_size entry, matching sccache's own config format.
